01 · Introduction

Hiring is broken on both sides of the market.

Candidates apply at scale but rarely learn why they were rejected. Recruiters drown in filters and still cannot identify the right fit with confidence. The missing layer is a feedback loop.

The candidate experience

Applying feels like a black box
  • Applications go out at scale, but replies are rare — many companies simply ghost candidates.
  • Rejections arrive without a reason, a score, or a concrete next step.
  • Resume iteration is guesswork: candidates do not know which signal to fix first.
  • Without feedback, the same mistakes repeat across every application.

The recruiter experience

Filters create noise, not signal
  • Legacy filters — age, college, category, experience — bury the genuinely relevant profiles.
  • No confidence score tells a recruiter how strongly a candidate actually fits the role.
  • No market baseline: recruiters over- or under-estimate what “good” looks like right now.
  • Manual screening is slow and exposed to unconscious bias.
talent.ai introduces the missing layer: verified profiles, blind-first review, AI confidence scoring, and structured feedback that turns every application into a learning signal.
02 · Problem Statement

A market that punishes iteration and rewards guessing.

The current hiring pipeline gives candidates no reason for rejection and gives recruiters no calibrated confidence in selection. Both sides are optimizing blind.

“In today’s job market, candidates apply to many companies but are ghosted or rejected without a reason — while recruiters apply filter after filter and still cannot find the candidate who truly fits the job description.

Candidate-side problem

  • No rejection reason → no path to improve the resume or profile.
  • Ghosting and generic emails erode trust in the process.
  • No way to know what the current market expects at a given experience level.

Recruiter-side problem

  • Filter overload hides the right candidate behind proxy attributes.
  • No confidence level or market baseline to calibrate expectations.
  • No structured mechanism to compare candidates fairly and consistently.
Research question: How can a candidate iteratively update their profile using structured market feedback — and how can a recruiter discover the right candidate with confidence, without bias or filter overload?
Wasted applications Longer time-to-hire Bias-prone screening Eroded candidate trust No feedback loop
03 · Literature Review

What prior work establishes — and what it leaves open.

Research has advanced résumé–job matching, person–job fit and fairness auditing. Few systems close the loop between recruiter feedback, candidate improvement and unbiased discovery.

Work Authors Key finding / gap
A Bibliometric Perspective on AI Research for Job–Résumé Matching 2022 S. Rojas-Galeano, J. Posada, E. Ordoñez Maps AI/NLP résumé–job matching research, its machine-learning themes and influential work. Shows a fragmented landscape with no closed feedback loop for candidates.
Person-Job Fit: Adapting the Right Talent for the Right Job with Joint Representation Learning 2018 C. Zhu, H. Zhu, H. Xiong, C. Ma, F. Xie, P. Ding, P. Li Uses a CNN to learn joint candidate–job representations from past applications and predict fit. Strong matching signal, but depends on historical application labels.
Mitigating Bias in Algorithmic Hiring: Evaluating Claims and Practices 2020 M. Raghavan, S. Barocas, J. Kleinberg, K. Levy Examines fairness claims and bias in automated hiring. Argues for evidence-based evaluation, transparency and auditable practices — not just accuracy.
Enhancing Person-Job Fit for Talent Recruitment: An Ability-aware Neural Network Approach 2018 C. Qin, H. Zhu, T. Xu, C. Zhu, L. Jiang, E. Chen, H. Xiong Compares candidate experience with job requirements through an ability-aware model. Supports fit prediction, sourcing and recommendations.
Anonymous Résumés: An Effective Preselection Method? 2019 A. Lacroux, C. Martin-Lacroux Tests anonymous vs. standard applications. Effects are context-dependent; anonymity neutralized some discrimination, supporting blind-first review.
Design and Development of a Machine Learning Based Resume Ranking System 2021 K. Tejaswini, V. Umadevi, S. M. Kadiwal, S. Revanna Automates résumé parsing, classification and ranking against a job description using content similarity and KNN. No recruiter feedback signal.
Fairness and Bias in Algorithmic Hiring: A Multidisciplinary Survey 2025 A. Fabris et al. (8 authors) Surveys bias, fairness measures, datasets, mitigation approaches and legal considerations. Confirms fairness must be designed into the workflow.
Gap addressed by talent.ai: existing work optimizes matching accuracy or fairness in isolation. talent.ai unifies structured feedback, blind review, confidence scoring and a credit economy into one platform.

05 · Methodology — Domain Decomposition

Start with bounded contexts, not with layers.

Using Domain-Driven Design, the application was split into nine bounded contexts. Each context owns its model, its database and its lifecycle — and becomes an independently deployable service.

Identity & Access

auth-service
PostgreSQL talent_auth · users, roles, refresh sessions, audit

Talent Profile

talent-service
MongoDB talent_profiles · skills, experience, tier

Recruiter & Jobs

recruiter-service
PostgreSQL talent_recruiter · orgs, jobs

Engagement

engagement-service
PostgreSQL talent_engagement · swipes, reviews

Rewards & Credits

rewards-service
PostgreSQL talent_rewards · wallet, ledger, unlocks

AI Matching

ai-matching-service
Qdrant + Redis · embeddings, TalentLens, cache

Notifications

notification-service
MongoDB + Redis · in-app, email, WebSocket

Analytics

analytics-service
PostgreSQL talent_analytics · read models, funnels

Edge & API

api-gateway
Redis · JWT, rate limits, circuit breakers, routing
Why this decomposition works: independent ownership · failure isolation · polyglot persistence · independent scaling · explicit REST and event contracts. The entire application is broken down into 9 services, each with its own datastore.

07 · Methodology — Containerization, Kubernetes & Observability

From source code to a self-observing cluster.

Every service is containerized, deployed through Kubernetes, and instrumented with structured logs, distributed traces and Prometheus metrics — using the same repeatable pattern.

Containerization

One image per service
  • Multi-stage Node 22 / Alpine build using a shared Dockerfile.service.
  • turbo prune installs only the dependencies a service needs; pnpm deploy produces a production-only bundle.
  • Runs as the unprivileged node user with tini as PID 1.
  • Unified Compose stack: PostgreSQL, MongoDB, Redis, RabbitMQ, Qdrant, MailHog, Jaeger, Prometheus, Grafana + all services.

Kubernetes

Declarative, scalable delivery
  • One Deployment + ClusterIP Service per microservice in the talent-ai namespace.
  • Shared ConfigMap and out-of-band Secret; mounted secret files supported via loadSecret().
  • Liveness and readiness probes back health checks and dependency verification.
  • HPA per service on CPU/memory; Nginx Ingress + TLS; Kustomize renders app + observability together.

Logging

Structured, correlated, searchable
  • Pino JSON logs with service and environment context.
  • The API gateway reuses or generates a correlation ID and forwards it downstream.
  • Every log line carries trace_id and span_id from the active OpenTelemetry span.
  • Audit logs for registration, login, refresh and logout; secrets loaded through mounted files.

Tracing & metrics

See every request end to end
  • OpenTelemetry starts before Express, Prisma, Redis and amqplib imports, capturing HTTP, DB, cache and broker spans.
  • OTLP/HTTP exports to Jaeger; the gateway injects a W3C traceparent so one trace spans gateway + service.
  • /metrics exposes RED metrics, domain events, AI provider health and Node process metrics.
  • 6 Grafana dashboards, 18 alert rules and runbooks; /health/liveness and /health/readiness back probes.
Code→ GitHub Actions→ GHCR images→ Kubernetes→ OTel → Jaeger Prometheus → Grafana Pino logs health probes + HPA

12 · Conclusion

Hiring should be a feedback loop, not a black box.

talent.ai connects candidate growth, recruiter confidence and cloud-native engineering into one platform — so every application produces a signal, and every signal makes the next decision better.

Candidates grow

AI summaries, concrete resume improvements and structured recruiter feedback replace silence with a path forward.

Recruiters decide with confidence

Blind review, semantic search and confidence scores reduce bias and filter overload while surfacing high-signal talent.

The platform stays observable

Nine containerized services on Kubernetes, with logging, tracing, metrics, dashboards, alerts and runbooks built in.
